extracted.intended_audience: exporters, license applicants, legal counsel, federal agencies, and stakeholders affected by U.S. sanctions and export-control policy
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice announcing determinations under the Chemical and Biological Weapons Control and Warfare Elimination Act of 1991 regarding Russia and the specific sanctions and licensing policies to be imposed, waived, or modified. The page communicates legal findings, statutory citations, the list of sanctions under section 307(a), and detailed license/exception policies and implementation instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of use of chemical weapons (22 U.S.C. 5604(a) / section 306(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to sections 306(a) ... the Acting Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs determined that the Government of the Russian Federation has used chemical or biological weapons in violation of international law or lethal chemical or biological weapons against its own nationals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This factual/legal determination is the statutory trigger for imposing sanctions under the Act. (Page notes the determination occurred on April 25, 2024.)

rubrics_metrics.name: 307(d) waiver—national security essential
rubrics_metrics.description: The Acting Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs has determined and certified to Congress pursuant to section 307(d) of the Act that it is essential to the national security interests of the United States to partially waive the application of the sanctions required under section 307(a) of the Act with respect to foreign assistance, licenses for the export of items on the U.S. Munitions List (USML), and the licensing of national security-sensitive goods and technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statutory waiver under 307(d) permits modifying or limiting the automatic application of section 307(a) sanctions in specific categories; the notice both asserts this certification and describes how waivers will operate for particular licensing categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of foreign assistance (section 307(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination of assistance to Russia under the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, except for urgent humanitarian assistance and food or other agricultural commodities or products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice states this sanction is imposed but also notes the Acting Under Secretary has determined it is essential to national security to waive the application of this restriction (see waiver discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of arms sales and USML export licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination of (a) sales to Russia under the Arms Export Control Act of any defense articles, defense services, or design and construction services, and (b) licenses for the export to Russia of any item on the United States Munitions List.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Acting Under Secretary has determined it is essential to national security to waive application of this sanction with respect to issuance of licenses in support of government space cooperation (reviewed case-by-case and consistent with prior export licensing policy for Russia). Licenses in support of commercial space launches shall be reviewed subject to a policy of denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of arms sales financing
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination of all foreign military financing for Russia under the Arms Export Control Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is listed as an independent sanction imposed under section 307(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of U.S. Government credit or other financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Denial to Russia of any credit, credit guarantees, or other financial assistance by any department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States Government, including the Export-Import Bank of the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies broadly to government-provided financial assistance instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on exports of national security-sensitive goods & technology (50 U.S.C. 4813(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibition on the export to Russia of any goods or technology controlled for National Security reasons on the control list established under 50 U.S.C. 4813(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary of State has determined it is essential to national security to waive this sanction in specified ways and replace it with a set of license exceptions and narrowly circumscribed licensing policies described in the notice (see subsequent entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: License Exceptions allowed: GOV, ENC, BAG, TMP, AVS
rubrics_metrics.description: License Exceptions: Exports and re-exports of goods or technology eligible under License Exceptions GOV, ENC, BAG, TMP, and AVS are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These specific EAR license exceptions are identified as permitted notwithstanding the general prohibition; applicants should consult the relevant exception definitions and conditions in the EAR and follow standard submission requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety of flight licenses — case-by-case review
rubrics_metrics.description: Exports and re-exports of goods or technology pursuant to new licenses necessary for the safety of flight of civil fixed-wing passenger aviation, provided that applications for such licenses shall be reviewed on a case-by-case basis, consistent with export licensing policy for Russia prior to the date of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety-of-flight licenses are not categorically allowed; each application will be evaluated individually and must align with prior policy practice for Russia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deemed exports/reexports — case-by-case review
rubrics_metrics.description: Exports and re-exports of goods or technology pursuant to new licenses for deemed exports and re-exports to Russian nationals, provided that applications for such licenses shall be reviewed on a case-by-case basis, consistent with export licensing policy for Russia prior to the date of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deemed export licenses to Russian nationals will be evaluated individually and under prior policy criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exports to wholly‑owned U.S. and other foreign subsidiaries — case-by-case review
rubrics_metrics.description: Exports and re-exports of goods or technology pursuant to new licenses for exports and re-exports to wholly-owned U.S. and other foreign subsidiaries in Russia, provided that applications for such licenses shall be reviewed on a case-by-case basis, consistent with export licensing policy for Russia prior to the date of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits limited licensing for wholly-owned subsidiaries but stresses individual review consistent with prior policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government space cooperation licenses — case-by-case review
rubrics_metrics.description: Exports and re-exports of goods or technology pursuant to new licenses in support of government space cooperation, provided that applications for such licenses shall be reviewed on a case-by-case basis, consistent with export licensing policy for Russia prior to the date of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government-to-government space cooperation licensing is permitted only with individualized review consistent with prior policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial space launches — policy of denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Exports and re-exports of goods or technology pursuant to new licenses in support of commercial space launches, will be reviewed subject to a policy of denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial space launch license applications should be expected to be denied as a general policy, absent extraordinary justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial end-users for civil end-uses — case-by-case with presumption of denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Exports and re-exports of goods or technology pursuant to new licenses for commercial end-users for civil end-uses in Russia unless they are wholly-owned U.S. or other foreign subsidiaries in Russia, provided that applications for such licenses will be reviewed on case-by-case basis and subject to a 'presumption of denial' policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial civil end-use license requests (other than to wholly-owned subsidiaries) face a presumption of denial and require strong justification to overcome it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to Department of Commerce EAR restrictions (15 CFR parts 744 and 746)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department of Commerce has implemented additional restrictions against Russia in response to its invasion of Ukraine. For the most current information about these restrictions, please see the Export Administration Regulations, e.g., 15 CFR parts 744 and 746. Also see https://www.bis.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and practitioners should consult the EAR and BIS guidance for complementary or additional controls and procedures that may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation period: measures effective for at least one year and until further notice
rubrics_metrics.description: These measures shall be implemented by the responsible departments and agencies of the United States government and will remain in place for at least one year and until further notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates minimum duration and that continuation depends on further notice; agencies should plan accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural/official-publication guidance: PDF is official edition; comments closed
rubrics_metrics.description: This document has been published in the Federal Register. Use the PDF linked in the document sidebar for the official electronic format. Comments are no longer being accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov is informational only and does not provide legal notice; users should verify against the official PDF on govinfo.gov. Public comments cannot be submitted for this notice (see DATES).
